A producer is an agent that contributes metadata to an XML Registry so a term gets maximum semantic understanding as it appears in an XML document. To do that, the producer has to be able to receive XML registry forms, submit metadata along with the related information resource artifacts, and notify. The system should produce and display submittal forms from the web as part of the Information Resource Submittal Package, which holds these artifacts: the XML Tag Specification, the XML Spec, meaning a DTD, DCD and so on, and a sample XML document of the tag being submitted. That package gets compressed and either emailed or sent by ftp to an addressee. Producers also download that package from the web, with forms, instructions and tools for submitting to the XML Registry. They submit the prescribed metadata, information resource type, information resource association, status code, data types specified and the other information in Appendix A, across a combination of forms, which again are part of that same package with the same three artifacts, compressed and emailed or ftp'd to an addressee. Submission should work through an on-line interactive process and also an off-line and interactive batch process. Then the system parses the submitted XML Registry specification forms and populates the XML Registry database. It needs to allow modifying specified terms and definitions of metadata and the status of Information Resources, and associating Information Resources as specified in Appendix A. Annotating rejected ones, that's a question mark for now. It should assemble registered information resources into new components, assemble new DTDs from current ones, and produce a DTD as an instantiation for the modeling environment, the other instantiations being database schema and message definition. It should notify on changes to Information Resources or to the authorized producer of a tag, let people post planned changes to a registry, approve and reject submissions, and forward a request to a different registry."},{"id":"M2:T10","text":"Let me play that back. The Information Resource Submittal Package comes from the web with forms, instructions and tools, and holds the XML Tag Specification, the XML Spec like DTD or DCD, and a sample XML document of the tag, compressed and emailed or sent by ftp to an addressee. Submitted metadata covers information resource type, association, status code, data types and the rest of Appendix A, through a combination of forms, either on-line interactive or off-line and interactive batch. The system parses the forms, populates the registry database, allows modifying terms, definitions and status, associates resources per Appendix A, maybe annotates rejections, which is still open, assembles registered resources into new components and new DTDs from current ones, produces a DTD as an instantiation for the modeling environment alongside database schema and message definition, notifies on changes to resources or the authorized producer of a tag, posts planned changes, approves and rejects submissions, and forwards requests to a different registry. Is that right?"},{"id":"M2:T11","text":"Yes, that's it."},{"id":"M2:T12","text":"And then the consumer side. A consumer looks through a registry to pick a tag structure to reuse in one or more applications that exchange data under a pre-defined agreement. For discovery, I need to see XML Tags with these relationships: ancestor and descendant, so a tag's origin; uses and used by, so a complex Container Tag's parent and child relationship; data type info, so a tag's data type and related information; versioning, so an Information Resource's versions; reference sets, so text related to the domain values or the related reference set; and amplifying information, other resources like ERwin models, DTDs, documents and so on. I want to view tags as a tree or hierarchy, or in a tabular format, with multiple search options to find a specific tag, plus a search to find all tags of a given subscriber or author. Every Information Resource gets its own web page showing all its pertinent information, based on its information resource type. I should be able to view the Information Resource Submittal Package with the XML Tag Specification, the XML Spec like DTD or DCD, and a sample XML document of the tag. An XML Tag Specification form gets displayed to the author of a given information resource, and that's used to input the requested information for that resource. I need to download the XML Tags or other selected Information Resources. The system should catalog entities and attributes within servers so you can browse, search and retrieve data related to XML sources, and process ANSI standard SQL as specified in FIPS PUB 127-2. It should establish rules for maximum semantic understanding of a term as it appears in an XML document, have links to DTDs, DCDs and Namespace, and let you subscribe to notifications of changes to Communities of Interest, COE, or to Information Resources."},{"id":"M2:T13","text":"Okay, noted."},{"id":"M2:T14","text":"Let's talk registry services.
